title: Cessna 210 N Centurion — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency procedures for the Cessna 210 N Centurion with Continental TSIO-520 turbocharged engine, constant-speed propeller, and retractable tricycle gear. Memory items are marked. All airspeeds and numeric limits must come from the specific aircraft POH. The TSIO-520 is fuel-injected — no carburetor icing. Retractable gear requires specific gear-unsafe procedures. Not a substitute for recurrent emergency training or qualified instruction.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the type.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, manifold pressure limits, or other numerical limitations — all must come from the specific aircraft POH.
Equipment and avionics vary widely across 210 N airframes. Verify every item against the specific aircraft and its POH before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

sections.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff — Before or At Liftoff

items.text: Brakes — apply firmly to stop within remaining runway
If airborne with insufficient altitude for return — land ahead
items.response: MAINTAIN WINGS LEVEL; LAND ON AVAILABLE SURFACE AHEAD OR WITHIN NARROW ANGLE OF RUNWAY HEADING
items.detail: Do not attempt to turn back to the runway at low altitude. The 210 does not glide well with gear extended; if gear is up and landing is immediate, leave it up.

sections.title: Engine Failure After Takeoff — Airborne, Low Altitude

items.text: Landing area — select a suitable surface ahead within glide range
items.response: SELECTED; DO NOT TURN BACK BELOW SAFE ALTITUDE
FULL — attempt restart if time permits

items.text: If restart fails — secure engine and prepare for forced landing
Landing gear — extend only when landing is assured on the chosen surface
Landing area — identify best available field within glide range

items.response: BOTH — confirm ON; try START if engine windmilling

items.text: Mayday call — squawk 7700; declare emergency on 121.5 or local frequency
If engine does not restart — secure and prepare for forced landing

items.response: FULL OPEN — to exhaust any residual fuel
OFF — deny cockpit air from engine compartment

items.text: Airspeed — increase to slip speed or dive per POH to blow out fire
Emergency descent — if fire persists, descend at maximum safe speed; declare Mayday

items.response: PREPARE FOR PRECAUTIONARY OR FORCED LANDING

items.text: Throttle — close; crank engine with starter to draw fire back into induction
items.response: THROTTLE CLOSED; STARTER ENGAGED IF FIRE IS INDUCTION-ONLY
ALL OCCUPANTS CLEAR; MOVE UPWIND OF AIRCRAFT
USE FROM UPWIND IF FIRE IS ACCESSIBLE WITHOUT RISK; CALL 911 / AIRPORT FIRE

items.text: Vents — open to clear smoke; do not open if smoke increases
Circuit breakers — identify the faulted circuit; do not reset a hot breaker
If fire extinguished — restore essential electrical items one at a time
items.response: RESTORE ITEMS SELECTIVELY; MONITOR FOR RECURRENCE

items.text: Master switch — restore if needed for safe flight; monitor for repeat fault
Power — reduce immediately to minimum necessary for flight
Oil pressure gauge and oil temperature — monitor both
items.response: CHECK BOTH; LOW PRESSURE WITH RISING TEMP INDICATES IMMINENT FAILURE

items.text: Land as soon as possible — do not delay; engine seizure may be imminent
Mayday — declare emergency if engine failure expected
If oil pressure reads zero but temperature remains normal, the gauge or sender may be faulty. Treat as engine failure and land immediately regardless — do not continue flight.
Airspeed — establish and maintain best glide speed
Landing field — select the best available surface; plan to arrive high rather than low
Mayday — squawk 7700; transmit position and intentions on 121.5 or last ATC frequency
Landing gear — extend only when landing is assured on the chosen field; leave retracted for off-airport soft-field landing if preferred per POH
items.response: DOWN AND LOCKED (three green) OR RETRACTED AS APPROPRIATE

items.text: Flaps — extend on final when field is made
Doors — unlatch before touchdown to prevent jamming
Occupants — brief to brace for impact

sections.title: Gear Unsafe / Abnormal Gear Indication
sections.condition: One or more gear position lights not showing green after gear handle placed DOWN

items.text: Go-around — do not land with abnormal gear indication
Gear handle — cycle UP then DOWN; allow full travel time
Gear warning horn — note whether it sounds with throttle reduced
Circuit breaker for gear system — check; reset once if tripped
Low airspeed and high-G maneuver — a brisk coordinated turn may dislodge stuck gear
items.response: ATTEMPT IF ALTITUDE PERMITS PER POH

items.text: ATC — advise of gear problem; request fly-by for tower visual confirmation if available
items.response: ATC NOTIFIED; FLY-BY REQUESTED IF APPLICABLE

items.text: If gear does not indicate down — follow Emergency Gear Extension procedure
If gear still unsafe after all attempts — land with minimum runway required; use foam or grass if available; keep occupants advised
items.response: PREPARED FOR BELLY LANDING IF REQUIRED

sections.title: Emergency Gear Extension (Manual Override)
sections.condition: Normal gear extension has failed to produce three-green indication

items.text: Airspeed — reduce to below gear extension speed
Manual gear extension — locate and operate the hand crank or manual release per POH for the specific aircraft
items.detail: The 210 N uses a hand-crank emergency extension system. Refer to the aircraft-specific POH for the exact location and number of turns required. The procedure varies by serial number and any STC modifications.

items.text: Allow time for gravity and airflow to extend and lock the gear
Gear warning horn — confirm silent with throttle at approach power and gear down
items.response: HORN SILENT (GEAR LOCKED) OR HORN SOUNDS (GEAR UNSAFE)

items.text: If three green — proceed with normal landing; land at minimum speed
items.response: CLEARED TO LAND; AVOID HARD TOUCHDOWN

items.text: If not three green — advise ATC; prepare for gear-up landing
items.response: ATC NOTIFIED; FOAM REQUESTED IF AVAILABLE; OCCUPANTS BRIEFED
